question: What is the primary purpose of a two-way referral system in mental health care?

options.A: To ensure seamless movement of patients and continuity of care across different levels
options.B: To permanently transfer patients away from community care settings
options.C: To eliminate the need for primary healthcare workers in mental health
options.D: To restrict patient access to tertiary psychiatric hospitals

explanation: The two-way referral system ensures smooth transitions and continuity of care between different healthcare levels, preventing gaps in treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h1)

question: What role do psychiatric nurses frequently play within the referral framework?

options.A: Acting as a bridge between patients, families, and multidisciplinary teams
options.B: Determining the budget for tertiary mental health institutions
options.C: Replacing community health extension workers entirely
options.D: Isolating patients from their local communities

explanation: Psychiatric nurses act as a vital bridge connecting patients, their families, and various healthcare teams across different levels of the system. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is a primary objective of psychiatric referrals?

options.A: To match the patient's clinical needs with the appropriate level of expertise
options.B: To increase the workload of primary healthcare workers
options.C: To keep patients in tertiary facilities indefinitely

explanation: A main objective of referrals is to ensure patients receive care that matches their clinical needs with the right level of expertise and resources. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why is patient and caregiver involvement important during the referral process?

options.A: It respects their autonomy and reduces apprehension
options.B: It makes them legally responsible for hospital administration
options.C: It eliminates the need for nursing documentation
options.D: It speeds up the discharge of medication stocks

explanation: Involving patients and caregivers respects their autonomy, keeps them informed, and helps reduce any fear or apprehension regarding the transition. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary level of care in the Nigerian healthcare system typically responsible for?

options.A: Serving as the first point of contact and providing basic mental health education

explanation: Primary health care centers serve as the first point of contact, offering basic mental health education, screening, and community-based support. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which facilities constitute the tertiary level of mental health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospitals and university teaching hospitals

explanation: Tertiary facilities include Federal Neuro-Psychiatric Hospitals and university teaching hospitals that offer highly specialized psychiatric care. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h3)

question: When is an upward referral process initiated in mental health care?

options.A: When patient needs exceed the capabilities of primary or secondary facilities
options.B: When a patient requests a change of hospital wardrobe
options.C: When the primary facility has an excess of empty beds
options.D: When the patient is completely cured and ready for discharge

explanation: Upward referrals are triggered when a patient's clinical needs surpass what primary or secondary healthcare facilities can safely manage. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h4)

question: What key document must accompany a patient during an upward referral?

options.A: A detailed referral letter outlining history, treatments, and reason for transfer
options.B: A receipt for hospital registration fees
options.C: A discharge certificate from community elders
options.D: A list of personal financial assets

explanation: A comprehensive referral letter detailing clinical history, medications, and the reason for referral is essential for safe and continuous care. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of the downward referral process?

options.A: To reintegrate stabilized patients into community care and primary facilities
options.B: To isolate chronic patients from their families permanently
options.C: To test new experimental drugs on unsuspecting patients
options.D: To increase congestion in tertiary psychiatric wards

explanation: Downward referrals return stabilized patients to community care, promoting social reintegration and reducing unnecessary institutionalization. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h5)

question: How do psychiatric nurses support the downward referral process?

options.A: By conducting family education, assessing homes, and establishing local linkages
options.B: By hiding medication schedules from family members
options.C: By discouraging patients from visiting primary health centers
options.D: By discharging patients without any clinical documentation

explanation: Nurses support downward referrals through family education, home assessments, medication preparation, and linking patients to local health centers. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following describes a clinical role of the psychiatric nurse in referrals?

options.A: Assessing the patient's condition and identifying red flags for escalation
options.B: Purchasing medical equipment for tertiary hospitals
options.C: Drafting national health policies for the ministry

explanation: Clinically, nurses assess patient conditions, identify red flags, and determine when care needs to be escalated or de-escalated. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h6)

question: How do psychiatric nurses act as educators during the referral process?

options.A: By preparing patients and families, explaining transitions, and offering psychoeducation
options.B: By teaching university nursing undergraduate classes exclusively
options.C: By withholding information to keep patients calm
options.D: By conducting medical school entrance examinations

explanation: Nurses educate patients and families by explaining what to expect during transitions and providing vital psychoeducation on self-care and medications. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is a major systemic barrier to effective mental health referrals in Nigeria?

options.A: Shortages of trained mental health personnel and poor infrastructure
options.B: An excess of psychiatric nurses at primary health centers
options.C: Overabundance of free emergency transport vehicles

explanation: Systemic challenges such as staff shortages, poor infrastructure, and lack of transport severely hinder effective referrals. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h7)

question: How do socio-cultural factors impact the referral process?

options.A: Stigma and reliance on alternative healers often cause patients to delay or default on care
options.B: They ensure 100% adherence to psychiatric appointments
options.C: They eliminate all financial constraints for patients
options.D: They force traditional healers to collaborate with tertiary hospitals

explanation: Widespread stigma and preference for alternative healing homes frequently lead to delayed care-seeking and default on formal referrals. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h7)

question: How can mobile health (mHealth) and tele-psychiatry improve community psychiatry coordination?

options.A: By allowing remote primary care nurses to consult directly with tertiary psychiatrists
options.B: By replacing all physical hospitals with virtual chatrooms
options.C: By eliminating the need for psychiatric nurses altogether
options.D: By preventing patients from communicating with their families

explanation: mHealth and tele-psychiatry bridge geographical divides, enabling real-time consultations between remote primary care nurses and tertiary specialists. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h8)

question: What is the benefit of integrating mental health into primary healthcare training programs?

options.A: It equips frontline nurses and workers with skills to manage conditions and navigate referrals
options.B: It ensures that primary workers can perform neurosurgery
options.C: It removes the need for patient documentation
options.D: It centralizes all psychiatric care exclusively in tertiary hospitals

explanation: Training equips frontline workers with necessary psychiatric competencies and knowledge of effective referral channels. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h8)
